issue.body:

rename.from: Using a PHP class constant for a key in a YAML hash as a method argument produces an ParseException
rename.to: Using a PHP class constant for a key in a YAML hash as a method argument produces a ParseException

body:
Thank you for the example. This helped to reproduce it. It looks like the parser still doesn't handle constants well in all places.

For example, this doesn't work:

```yaml
App\Example:
    calls:
      - method: addOptions
        arguments:
          - !php/const App\Example::CONSTANT_1: 'value_0'
            key_1: "value_1"
            key_2: "value_2"
```

while this parses correctly:

```yaml
App\Example:
    calls:
      - method: addOptions
        arguments:
          - key_1: "value_1"
            !php/const App\Example::CONSTANT_1: 'value_0'
            key_2: "value_2"
```

Absolutely, I wasn't really sure what was wrong so I just tried to give the detail that I had at least.

Oh neat!! I didn't realize that that syntax existed for invoking methods, that's so much better! And thanks for the explanation, I reproduced it and have a much clearer understanding of what is wrong now.

Thanks a ton for tracking this down @xabbuh, really appreciated.
Thank you for providing this very good example that allows to reproduce it. I don't know how hard it will be to fully fix this, but now I at least have some test input for the parser. 😃

issue.title: [Yaml] Fix for #36624; Allow PHP constant as first key in block
issue.body:
| Q             | A
| ------------- | ---
| Branch?       | 3.4
| Bug fix?      | yes
| New feature?  | no
| Deprecations? | no
| Tickets       | Fix #36624 
| License       | MIT
| Doc PR        | 

When using a PHP constant in the first key of a mapping the parser would throw an exception. However if you used a PHP constant in any other key but the first it was allowed. This fix allows PHP constant as the first key.

I've included a test for this parser error along with the fix.

issue.title: Move PS Accounts services in common service container
issue.body:
Fixes

`
The service "PrestaShop\Module\PrestashopFacebook\Factory\PsApiClientFactory" has a dependency on a non-existent service "PrestaShop\PsAccountsInstaller\Installer\Facade\PsAccounts".
`

hapenning on front office, caused by services available in back office only.

The following error has been fixed too, by hard coding the version of PS Accounts in the YML instead of using the `!php/const` that seems to be causing issues in some cases: https://github.com/symfony/symfony/issues/36624
`Fatal error: Uncaught Symfony\Component\Yaml\Exception\ParseException: The constant "PrestaShop\Module\PrestashopFacebook\Config\Config::COMPLIANT_PS_ACCOUNTS_VERSION" is not defined at line 5 (near "- !php/const PrestaShop\Module\PrestashopFacebook\Config\Config::COMPLIANT_PS_ACCOUNTS_VERSION"). in /var/www/html/vendor/symfony/symfony/src/Symfony/Component/Yaml/Inline.php:725 Stack trace: #0 /var/www/html/vendor/symfony/symfony/src/Symfony/Component/Yaml/Inline.php(363): Symfony\Component\Yaml\Inline::evaluateScalar('!php/const Pres...', 768, Array) #1 /var/www/html/vendor/symfony/symfony/src/Symfony/Component/Yaml/Inline.php(126): Symfony\Component\Yaml\Inline::parseScalar('!php/const Pres...', 768, NULL, 92, true, Array) #2 /var/www/html/vendor/symfony/symfony/src/Symfony/Component/Yaml/Parser.php(774): Symfony\Component\Yaml\Inline::parse('!php/const Pres...', 768, Array) #3 /var/www/html/vendor/symfony/symfony/src/Symfony/Component/Yaml/Parser.php(244): Symfony\Component\Yaml\Parser->parseValue('!php/const Pres...', in /var/www/html/vendor/symfony/symfony/src/Symfony/Component/Config/Loader/FileLoader.php on line 168`


This issue could be fixed on Symfony 3.4.44, but PS 1.7.7.4 use v3.4.37.
